abstract: We present a lightweight memory arena for PHP that embeds a Chronos-driven allocation policy and a balanced indexing mechanism for free blocks. The arena maintains a contiguous byte array and a free list sorted by offset, enabling first-fit allocation and deallocation with constant-time updates. We prove that the free list invariant---no overlap and sorted offsets---holds after every operation and that the amortized cost of allocation and deallocation is $O(\log n)$ where $n$ is the number of free blocks, following the analysis of Tarjan \cite{Tarjan_1985_AmortizedComplexity}. Empirical evaluation on an AMD EPYC 9V45 system yields a mean latency of 31 440.93 \textmu{}s and a throughput of 31 806 ops/s over 30 iterations. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/php-backend-core/tree/main/algorithms/20261117_110131_aether-framework_in_the_memory}
